title: DMC3 HD functions parameterised by a constant, and the selector dispatch behind a pointer field

records.title: 1,311 calls pass a constant first argument, over 179 functions
records.summary: Tracking the constants the code puts in a register — an immediate move, a register cleared against itself, an address computation over a constant — makes the first argument readable wherever it is one. 1,311 call sites pass a constant, reaching 179 distinct functions. What the constant means is not stated by any of this; what is stated is which functions are parameterised by a small value and which values exist, which bounds an enumeration without naming it. The shapes differ and the difference is itself informative: the function at RVA 0x2C6D90 is called 202 times with 59 distinct values, RVA 0x1B82C0 93 times with 20 values densely filling one to twenty-one,, RVA 0x8BF30 59 times with 49 values scattered from 10 to beyond 135, and RVA 0x2E7CA0 180 times with only seven.

records.title: The function behind a pointer field dispatches on its first argument, read from the compare chain
records.summary: The function at RVA 0x2E7CA0, whose result 86 stores file into an object, was first called an allocator on weak signals and then a factory keyed by a selector. The second reading is now read rather than inferred. From RVA 0x2E7D20 it compares its first argument against zero, one, two and three in a chain of subtract-and-branch, calls a different function in each arm with the same four-argument shape, and returns null for anything else. The arms at RVA 0x2E3B10, 0x2EBA10 and 0x324460 are 125 bytes each and identical in shape, differing only in the address each loads into its own first argument: RVA 0xCAB230, 0xCAE7D0 and one more, all in writable data. So the first argument selects which of several identical routines runs, and what distinguishes them is a data address rather than a type. The 180 call sites pass seven distinct values, zero through three and eight, sixteen and sixty-four; only the first four reach an arm. The class of what comes back still does not follow from any of this, and saying so is the point: the chain is read, the meaning is not.

records.title: Correction: 130 functions take a constant first argument, not 179
records.summary: The figure of 1,311 calls over 179 functions was inflated by a decoder-level mistake. The x86-64 forms that carry their register inside the opcode — mov reg, immediate at B8 through BF among them — have no ModRM field to extend, so REX.B is the only thing distinguishing rax from r8 and rcx from r9. The register tracking read the low three bits without it, so `mov r9d, imm` recorded a constant in rcx, and the next call was reported as taking a constant first argument when it took nothing of the kind. Reading REX.B leaves 1,319 calls over 130 functions: the call count barely moves and the function count falls by 49, a twenty-seven per cent overstatement. The separate reading of the function at RVA 0x2E7CA0 is unaffected, because that one was read off its own compare chain rather than inferred from this census — which is the whole reason the compare chain was read.

locations.note: RVA 0x4C3D1, 41 B8 7C 02 00 00: mov r8d, 0x27C, read as a write to rax without REX.B.
